assertions_contracts.best_practice: C++26 adds standardised Contracts (pre/post/assert with evaluation semantics); libc++ hardening assertion semantics are explicitly modelled on C++26 Contracts semantics. Implementation lags the standard: Clang's status page lists Contracts as not yet implemented, GCC 16 has experimental support.
assertions_contracts.evidence: WG21's direction paper P5000R1 names reflection, contracts and std::execution as the headline C++26 completions; libc++ docs define ignore/observe/enforce/quick-enforce semantics 'based on C++26 Contracts evaluation semantics'.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: static_assert for compile-time facts, assert() for runtime invariants (NDEBUG caveat stated), span treated as a borrow not a bounds check; no contract facility, because the guide targets C++23.

bounded_work.best_practice: The philosophy is validated by the direction of the standard: C++26 adds std::inplace_vector, a fixed-capacity contiguous container, exactly the bounded-storage shape this guide hand-rolls under C++23.
bounded_work.evidence: GCC's C++ status tracking and GCC 16 release material list std::inplace_vector among the C++26 library additions with experimental implementation support; nothing official contradicts explicit budgets.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named constexpr budgets for counts, bytes, depth, retries and queues; growth and reserve() bounded before allocation; retries need idempotency and a shared deadline.

concurrency.best_practice: jthread + stop_token remains the sanctioned owned-thread model (the guide's own cited draft sections). C++26 extends the toolkit with std::execution (senders), hazard pointers and RCU, but none of it changes the guide's ownership/cancellation discipline.
concurrency.evidence: Clang's C++2c table shows the new concurrency-adjacent features still unimplemented in Clang, so jthread remains the only portable recommendation today.
concurrency.guide_position: Prefer std::jthread with an explicit cooperative stop-token protocol; data races are UB; volatile does not synchronise; coroutine frames need a named owner; bounded task count and queues.

error_handling.best_practice: std::expected is the standard C++23 vocabulary for expected failure and remains so in C++26; the C++ Core Guidelines sanction both exceptions (for errors that cannot be handled locally) and error codes/expected-style returns under a documented policy.
error_handling.evidence: The guide's cited draft specification for expected is the standardised C++23 facility; the Core Guidelines' error-handling section (E:) remains organised around a stated per-codebase policy, which is what the guide mandates.
error_handling.guide_position: One exception policy plus one typed expected-error policy per subsystem; std::expected<T,E> for routine domain failure, checked before value/error access; no exception crosses a C ABI boundary; exception guarantees documented.

formatting.best_practice: clang-format remains the reference formatter for C++; the four pinned options are current documented options. Values are house policy (LLVM base itself defaults to 2-space/80-col), which the guide presents as its own pin, not an upstream claim.
formatting.evidence: Current LLVM documentation still documents the .clang-format style mechanism and LLVM preset the pin is based on.
formatting.guide_position: Pinned clang-format: BasedOnStyle LLVM, IndentWidth 4, ColumnLimit 100, UseTab Never; headers self-contained; semantic rewrites run separately from formatting.

memory_ownership.best_practice: The C++ Core Guidelines' resource-management rules (R:) still prescribe exactly this: RAII, unique ownership by default, shared ownership only for genuine sharing, no raw owning pointers/new-delete in application code.
memory_ownership.evidence: Core Guidelines (living document, updated Jun 2026) continues to organise resource safety around RAII, leak-freedom and tool-enforced ownership - the same model; C++26's erroneous-behaviour and hardening work reinforces rather than replaces it.
memory_ownership.guide_position: RAII and Rule of Zero; unique_ptr for exclusive ownership, shared_ptr only for genuine shared ownership, cycles broken deliberately; nonthrowing destructors; explicit checked finish for fallible completion; views borrow and never extend lifetime.

security.best_practice: Standard-library hardening is now a first-class, vendor-documented defence the guide never mentions: libc++ offers none/fast/extensive/debug hardening modes (fast is explicitly recommended for production), C++26 standardises hardened-library semantics, and libstdc++ has its own assertion/hardening controls.
security.evidence: libc++ hardening docs: fast mode 'contains a set of security-critical checks... intended to be used in production. We recommend most projects adopt this'; failures in production modes trap immediately. This is a defence-in-depth layer complementary to, and cheaper than, the guide's sanitizer-only runtime story.
security.guide_position: Warnings plus ASan/UBSan in testing, review of casts/pointers/format strings/dynamic loading as trust boundaries, no std::system on external input, argv form.

static_analysis.best_practice: clang-tidy is the official enforcement vehicle: its cppcoreguidelines-* group mechanically checks the Core Guidelines, cert-* checks CERT, bugprone-* catches the exact lifetime/view mistakes this guide warns about (including capturing-this), and it runs the Clang Static Analyzer.
static_analysis.evidence: clang-tidy docs list cppcoreguidelines, cert, bugprone and clang-analyzer groups; the Core Guidelines are explicitly designed as targets for analysis tools. The guide references Core Guidelines only as a source for lifetime rules, never as a check set.
static_analysis.guide_position: SKILL pairing is clangd + clang-format + lldb-dap; the full guide says to use warnings, sanitizers and static analysis 'together' but names no analyzer, no check set and no CI step.

testing.best_practice: Consistent with Core Guidelines and sanitizer practice; current guidance adds hardened-library debug modes in CI (see security), but the guide's test matrix itself is not superseded.
testing.evidence: libc++ documents debug hardening mode as the mode for 'test suites, CI, or local development' - an addition to, not a replacement for, the guide's sanitizer testing.
testing.guide_position: Expected-error alternatives, empty/max views, sanitizer-driven lifetime tests, allocation/constructor failure, output preservation, exception guarantees, cancellation/destructor-join tests, release (NDEBUG) run with independent checks.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: C++23 remains the current published ISO standard on isocpp.org (ISO/IEC 14882:2024). C++26 was technically finalised in Mar 2026 (contracts/reflection/execution included) but ISO publication was still pending at the time isocpp.org was fetched, and compiler support is partial - Clang lists C++2c as Partial with Contracts and Reflection unimplemented.
toolchain_pins.evidence: isocpp.org 'The Standard' page (fetched for this audit) names C++23 as the current standard and C++26 as in-progress materials; Clang's status page confirms partial C++26 support. The C++23 pin is therefore current, with a dated migration horizon the guide should name.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: C++23 is the reference profile (std::expected); C++20 projects must supply an alternative result type; C++26 features must not be described as C++23 guarantees.

current_versions.C++ (ISO/IEC 14882): C++23 (ISO/IEC 14882:2024) is the current published standard per isocpp.org; C++26 technically finalised Mar 2026, ISO publication pending, implementation partial
current_versions.Clang/LLVM: LLVM 22.1.x series current; Clang status: C++23 Partial, C++2c (C++26) Partial, Contracts and Reflection not yet implemented
current_versions.GCC/libstdc++: GCC 16.1 (Apr 2026): C++20 library stable, C++ defaults to gnu++20, experimental C++26 features incl. contracts/reflection/inplace_vector
current_versions.clang-format: Ships with LLVM 22.1.x; pinned options all still valid
current_versions.clang-tidy: Current with LLVM 22.1.x; cppcoreguidelines-*, cert-*, bugprone-* groups; NOT paired in the guide
current_versions.clangd: Ships with LLVM 22.1.x; guide pairs it, version not pinned in guide
current_versions.libc++ hardening: none/fast/extensive/debug modes documented; fast recommended for production; vendor default is none unless configured

proposals.evidence: libc++ docs recommend the fast hardening mode for most production projects, extensive for broader checking, debug for CI/tests; vendor default is none, so a project that never names a mode gets no checking - precisely the silent gap in the guide's profile declaration step.
proposals.proposal: Add standard-library hardening to the profile declaration and build recipes: require each project to name its libc++ hardening mode (_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE fast in production, debug in tests) or the libstdc++ equivalent, exactly as it already names its exception policy.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: near-zero code cost, catches the container/iterator precondition violations the guide currently only reviews for.

proposals.evidence: P5000R1 confirms contracts completed C++26; Clang's status table lists P2900 Contracts as 'No', so the guide cannot switch yet - but libc++ already exposes contracts-style assertion semantics, showing the intended migration shape.
proposals.proposal: Add a C++26 migration note to the guide: contracts (P2900) are the designated successor to the assert-based contract style, to be adopted per-project when the pinned compiler implements them; until then keep assert/static_assert and do not backport contract syntax into the C++23 profile.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a documented watch item with a concrete trigger (pinned Clang/GCC implements P2900), not as an immediate style change.

proposals.evidence: clang-tidy's check-group list includes cppcoreguidelines and cert groups designed to enforce the two guideline sets the guide already cites as authorities.
proposals.proposal: Pair clang-tidy in the SKILL (cppcoreguidelines-*, bugprone-*, cert-*, clang-analyzer-*) alongside clangd, mirroring the recommendation made for the C guide so the two LLVM-based guides share one analyzer story.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt together with the C guide change for consistency.
